item.title: Addendum and Corrigendum to: Some homological properties of category $\mathcal{O}$, V
item.description: arXiv:2611.12892v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In various special cases, we provide an alternative argument for equivalence between Kostant positivity of some involutions in type $A$ and the conjunction of the categorical K{\aa}hrstr{\"o}m's condition for these involutions with indecomposability of the images of the corresponding simple modules in category $\mathcal{O}$ under projective functors.
item.dc:creator: Hankyung Ko, Volodymyr Mazorchuk

item.title: Geometric Hammocks: Surface Laminations and the Ziegler Spectrum of String Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.12931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give the first complete topological, geometric, and ergodic classification of the Ziegler spectrum $\Zg(\Lambda)$ of a non-domestic string algebra $\Lambda$ over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary cardinality, via a dictionary with Thurston's theory of geodesic laminations on a cusped hyperbolic surface. This is a model-theoretic counterpart of Haiden--Katzarkov--Kontsevich's realization (\emph{Publ.\ Math.\ IHES} 2017) of stability conditions on the bounded derived category of a gentle algebra via flat surfaces: pure-injective modules correspond to admissible geodesics, and the Ziegler topology to a corridor quotient of Chabauty space. Three consequences follow. The Krull--Gabriel dimension equals the surface's topological accumulation depth, and the string closure with all higher Cantor--Bendixson strata is globally homeomorphic to an explicit corridor space, with the pushout map to $\Zg(\Lambda)$ a homeomorphism if and only if $\Lambda$ is domestic. Prefix-free dyadic blocks in the geometric perfect core verify Puninski's cardinality-free two-chain criterion, resolving the open problem of superdecomposable pure-injectives over uncountable fields for all non-domestic string and special biserial algebras. Three purely algebraic invariants on the perfect core---localized pp-shape entropy, a $K_0$-weighted pressure function satisfying an algebraic Ruelle--Walters Variational Principle, and a pp-bifurcation index with a Gauss--Bonnet simplicity obstruction---strictly separate uncountable iso-entropic and iso-pressure families, and the inverse limit of the quotient pp-lattice recovers the transversal Cantor cross-section.
item.dc:creator: Shantanu Sardar

item.title: Representations of the Loop mirror BMS-Kac-Moody algebra
item.description: arXiv:2611.13025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we construct a new family of non-weight modules $\Omega(\lambda,\zeta,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\sigma, h)$ over the loop mirror BMS-Kac-Moody algebra $\mathcal{G}$, which is a Takiff-type extension of the loop mirror Heisenberg--Virasoro algebra. We establish criteria for irreducibility, determine their isomorphism classes, and classify all $\mathcal{G}$-modules that are free of rank one. Moreover, we determine all self-extensions of these modules: for every such module $M$, $\operatorname{Ext}^{1}_{U(\mathcal{G})}(M,M)\cong \mathbb{C}^{6}$, and we construct explicit $1$-cocycles realizing every cohomology class. Every nonsplit self-extension of a simple module is indecomposable of composition length two. Restricting these modules to the loop mirror Heisenberg--Virasoro subalgebra $\mathcal{H}$ yields new $\mathcal{H}$-modules. Among them the $\sigma$-type modules $\Psi(\lambda,\zeta,\sigma,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,h)$ constitute a new family with no counterpart in the non-loop or non-Takiff case. For the degenerate case $\sigma=0$, we establish criteria for irreducibility and isomorphism, and describe certain maximal submodules and their simple quotients. Finally, we construct and classify a new class of tensor product $\mathcal{H}$-modules.
item.dc:creator: Haibo Chen, Yongliang Wang, Ying Xu

item.title: A decomposition theorem for minimal W-algebras of type A
item.description: arXiv:2611.13239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To any simple Lie algebra, one can associate a minimal affine W-algebra. It is a vertex algebra which is obtained from the universal affine vertex algebra by a chiral Hamiltonian reduction procedure. This reduction is determined by data coming from the minimal nilpotent orbit. It is a chiral quantisation of the Slodowy slice associated to this minimal orbit. In this paper, when the simple Lie algebra is of type A, we prove that the minimal W-algebra is isomorphic to a commutant subalgebra in a localisation of the universal affine vertex algebra. Then, we establish a decomposition theorem \`a la Losev: the localised universal affine vertex algebra decomposes as the tensor product of the minimal affine W-algebra and another vertex subalgebra. As a direct corollary, we retrieve the celebrated result of inverse Hamiltonian reduction for the minimal W-algebra. We also prove an analogue of this result for the corresponding finite W-algebra. In both cases, our approach relies on the geometry of the associated Slodowy slice.
item.dc:creator: Thibault Juillard

item.title: G-radical-square-zero algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.13445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we first provide necessary and sufficient conditions for a Krull-Schmidt triangulated category with Auslander-Reiten triangles to have square-zero radical. One of these conditions is that the middle term of every Auslander-Reiten triangle is either zero or indecomposable. We then call an artin algebra {\it G-radical-square-zero} if the stable category of Gorenstein-projective modules has square-zero radical. We characterize when a G-radical-square-zero algebra is CM-finite and, in this case, give an additive generator of the stable category. For certain Iwanaga-Gorenstein G-radical-square-zero algebras, we further show that the stable category admits an additive generator consisting of higher syzygies of simple modules.
item.dc:creator: Takahiro Honma, Satoshi Usui

item.title: Differential Monodromy, $q$-Opers, and Universal $(G,q)$-Wronskians
item.description: arXiv:2611.13446v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a geometric formulation of the $q$DE/ODE/IM correspondence for families of differential operators associated with simple Lie algebras of ADE type. Under analytic hypotheses, the $q$-connection associated with shifted monodromy defines a twisted $(G,q)$-oper and has Steinberg form in the frame of solutions normalized by prescribed asymptotics in a sector at infinity. We identify the central connection between the normalized solution frames at zero and infinity with a universal meromorphic $(G,q)$-Wronskian. Its generalized minors give $Q$-functions satisfying the ADE $QQ$-relations. When $q$ is not a root of unity, we parametrize shifted monodromy by quantum-affine $q$-characters evaluated on shifted $Q$-ratios, using the same character formulas that describe normalized transfer-matrix eigenvalues. We verify the analytic hypotheses for generic untwisted Feigin--Frenkel--Hernandez affine opers, thereby relating these affine opers to twisted $(G,q)$-opers.
item.dc:creator: Anton M. Zeitlin

item.title: Regular loci of affine Springer fibers at very special parahoric level
item.description: arXiv:2611.13601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For split groups, we prove that centralizers act transitively on regular loci of affine Springer fibers at very special parahoric level. As an application, we prove Chi's conjecture on the number of top-dimensional irreducible components of affine Lusztig varieties.
item.dc:creator: Ryosuke Shimada

item.title: Finite Numerical Joyce Transport and Derived Hall Scattering Groupoid
item.description: arXiv:2611.13761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{D}$ be a triangulated category over a finite field $k$ satisftying certain finiteness conditions. Let $\Sigma$ be a connected component of the space of numerical stability conditions on $\mathcal{D}$ with one element $\sigma\in\Sigma$ satisfying the support property and the finite counting condition. We prove that each of the Joyce elements with respect to $\sigma_1\in\Sigma$ is a finite rational Lie polynomial in those of any other $\sigma_0\in\Sigma$, so the generated Lie subalgebra $\mathfrak{L}_\sigma,\sigma\in\Sigma$ in the uncompleted derived Hall algebra $\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{D})$ is constant on $\Sigma$. Our proof combines completions on strict sectors with a uniform mass bound for successive local substitutions. We use the method of Hall scattering diagrams on phase categories to provide a realization of the transform of Joyce elements. For the finite-length case, we also give an alternative proof using finite-length hearts instead of phase categories. As an application, we explicit the generators of the Lie subalgebra $\mathfrak{L}$ in the Dynkin case.
item.dc:creator: Wenyu Gao, Fan Xu

item.title: E-symmetric algebras II
item.description: arXiv:2611.13889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce generalized Jacobian algebras and show that a finite-dimensional algebra is E-symmetric if and only if it is generalized Jacobian. We also characterize E-symmetric algebras in terms of its simple modules. We show that Enomoto's counterexample to the Periodicity Conjecture is a generalized Jacobian algebra, which is not Jacobian in the classical sense.
item.dc:creator: Grzegorz Bobi\'nski, Carolin Hartung, Jan Schr\"oer

item.title: On the strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence for the quantum semisimple groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.13897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence, when it holds for an algebra, characterizes its primitive ideals ( that is, the annihilators of irreducible representations) both algebraically and topologically within the prime spectrum. A stronger form, known as the strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence, was introduced by Bell, Launois, and Nolan in their work on 'A strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence for quantum Schubert cells'. In this paper, we prove that the generic quantized coordinate rings of connected, simply connected semisimple complex algebraic groups satisfy the strong Dixmier-Moeglin equivalence.
item.dc:creator: Nirina Albert Razafimandimby

item.title: High degree covers and genericity
item.description: arXiv:2611.13988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is known that the genuine irreducible Iwahori-spherical representations of a tame $n$-fold Brylinski-Deligne cover of a $p$-adic split connected reductive group are all generic, when the degree $n$ is suitably large. This has been established by studying the the structure of the Gelfand-Graev representation as a module under the action of the Iwahori-Hecke algebra. In this paper, we present a different proof based on metaplectic Moy-Prasad theory.
item.dc:creator: Edmund Karasiewicz

item.title: Gorenstein dimensions for stable Auslander algebras of Nakayama algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.14057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A$ be a Nakayama algebra and $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$ its stable Auslander algebra. We introduce a new homological invariant, called the finitistic Gorenstein dimension, which coincides with the classical Gorenstein dimension whenever the latter is finite, and compute this invariant for $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$ when $A$ has infinite global dimension. Combined with an accompanying criterion for the finiteness of the Gorenstein dimension of $\underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A)$, our results provide a complete description of this dimension and verify the Gorenstein Symmetry Conjecture for this class of algebras. Furthermore, we show that the finitistic Gorenstein dimension of $ \underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A) $ is also left-right symmetric, is explicitly related to the finitistic dimension of $A$, and can be attained among the injective dimensions of the projective $ \underline{\mathrm{Aus}}(A) $-modules corresponding to simple $A$-modules. Our proofs rely on computing injective dimensions in terms of distances in the coresolution forest of $A$, a combinatorial structure closely related to Ringel's coresolution quiver.
item.dc:creator: Odysseas Giatagantzidis, Carolin Hartung, Nupur Jain, Ren\'e Marczinzik, Martin Rubey, Sven Schmitz

item.title: Parabolic induction and pullback of perverse sheaves on Vogan varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.14156v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be a Levi subgroup of a quasisplit connected reductive group $G$ over a $p$-adic field. Vogan's geometric perspective on the local Langlands correspondence fixes a perfect pairing between the Grothendieck group of representations of $G$ and its pure inner forms with a fixed infinitesimal parameter and the Grothendieck group of equivariant perverse sheaves on the associated Vogan variety. Granting a list of desiderata for the enhanced local Langlands correspondence, we show that parabolic induction $\mathrm{Ind}_M^G$ is the transpose of geometric restriction $\xi^*$ with respect to this pairing if and only if the $p$-adic analogue of the Kazhdan--Lusztig hypothesis and the expected multiplicity formula for tempered induction both hold. The identity refines to one for each pure inner form of $G$.
item.dc:creator: Chi-Heng Lo, Mishty Ray

item.title: Whittaker supermodules for the Takiff superalgebra \mathfrak{osp}(1|2)
item.description: arXiv:2611.14303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we classify all simple Whittaker supermodules over the Takiff Lie superalgebra \(\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)\otimes\mathbb C[t]/(t^2)\), associated with Whittaker characters defined on the even part of its positive nilpotent subalgebra.
item.dc:creator: Wei Wang, Yongjie Wang, Chuchao Xu

item.title: Parabolic semiinfinite sheaves on affine flag varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.14378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study sheaves on affine flag varieties of reductive algebraic groups in parabolic semiinfinite settings, generalizing some constructions and results from the work of Gaitsgory and of Achar, Dhillon, and the first author (for the case of the Borel subgroup) and of Dhillon and Lysenko (for characteristic-$0$ coefficients and a particular case of parabolic semiinfinite condition). In particular we define perverse t-structures and Raskin equivalences in this context, and study an analogue of the Gaitsgory sheaf. In future work, these $\infty$-categories will be related to representation-theoretic $\infty$-categories associated with the Langlands dual group.
item.dc:creator: Simon Riche, Quan Situ

item.title: Multivariate diagonal harmonics: character polynomials and proofs of two conjectures of Bergeron
item.description: arXiv:2611.00629v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove Bergeron's Hook-Components and Coefficient-Length conjectures for the Vandermonde polarization module and full diagonal harmonics in every rank and number of alphabets. Hook-label characters are elementary skewings of the alternating character, and the maximal Schur length in label $\mu$ is $n-\mu_1$. We compute character and dimension polynomials of diagonal coinvariants in every bosonic--fermionic superspace for $D\ge3$, $n\ge\max\{D,2D-6\}$, answering Church--Ellenberg--Farb's character and dimension questions. For augmented commutative algebras in characteristic zero, we construct natural two-Schur presentations and filtered free resolutions with one Schur generator in each homological degree. For polynomial algebras, specialization to orthogonal idempotents identifies the first unstable correction for every nonempty tail $\tau$ and degree $D>|\tau|$. The stable threshold $n\ge D+\tau_1$ is sharp when the row dimension is at least $\ell(\tau)$. First parabolic algebras recover finite jets, their multiplication and their maps. Selected-label lifts give uniform Vandermonde generation through degree $D$ for $D\ge3$, $n\ge2D-3$, and disjoint-label products generate every first occurrence for positive integral row weights. Constructive degree reflection determines all two-column moment homology and generates its first syzygies from degree $n+1$; two-column Vandermonde generation reduces to degree $n-1$. Invariants and harmonics separate through the character range and through degree $n$ in two alphabets. The hook identities also give the fully graded sign component of the $t=0$, $(1,2)$-superspace Theta conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Eren Ercan

item.title: Koszul duality and determinant formulas for affine hyperplane arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2611.13050v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For real affine hyperplane arrangements, we prove Lam's determinant conjecture for the inverse Varchenko matrix restricted to bounded chambers. The proof combines Lam's comparison of twisted intersection forms with the period determinant formula of Varchenko, Loeser-Sabbah and Douai-Terao. For normal crossing arrangements, we introduce the taut path algebra and the chamber intersection algebra and establish a Koszul duality between them, yielding an explicit multivariate formula for the inverse Varchenko matrix. After specializing the parameters to $q$, its restriction to bounded chambers is a scalar multiple of the $q$-intersection matrix, proving a determinant conjecture of the authors. We also discuss how the Koszul duality results generalize to affine oriented matroids.
item.dc:creator: Jens Niklas Eberhardt, Carl Mautner

item.title: Cluster-theoretic Newton--Okounkov polytopes of flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.13385v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Newton--Okounkov bodies have been used for studying toric degenerations of flag varieties. We classify the Newton--Okounkov polytopes associated with cluster valuations and the anticanonical line bundle on full flag varieties of types $A_4$ and $B_2$. In type $A_4$, the $672$ seeds of cluster type $D_6$ yield $162$ affine unimodular equivalence classes, which coincide with the combinatorial equivalence classes. We determine the subgroup of exchange-graph automorphisms preserving every polytope class. It is a Klein four group of index six in the automorphism group of the exchange graph of cluster type $D_6$. In type $B_2$, we give defining inequalities for all six seeds. At the anticanonical weight, the two combinatorial equivalence classes split into three affine unimodular equivalence classes. Their respective class-preserving automorphism groups have orders four and two.
item.dc:creator: Shin Hong, Jeongsoo Kim, Eunjeong Lee

item.title: Quantum Langlands correspondence for Painlev\'e II
item.description: arXiv:2611.13639v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct an irregular KZ-BPZ correspondence for quantum Painlev\'e II from a rank-three Wakimoto-Whittaker module. The irregular KZ equation and the quantum isomonodromy equation form a joint affine system whose Drinfeld-Sokolov reduction yields scalar BPZ equations. We obtain matrix-integral solutions of this system for one fundamental insertion. An exact quantum Langlands duality exchanges the fundamental insertion with the zero of the dual Whittaker differential and allows affine solutions to be reconstructed from the BPZ equations. This duality interchanges the classical and Nekrasov-Shatashvili limits, which yield the Painlev\'e II Lax connection and an irregular Gaudin oper, respectively.
item.dc:creator: Sibasish Banerjee, Babak Haghighat, Jie Sun

item.title: Local Rigidity of Bergman Logarithmic Flatness on Compact Hermitian Symmetric Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.14507v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the local rigidity of Bergman logarithmic flatness near the standard metrics associated with fixed invariant positive polarizations on compact Hermitian symmetric spaces. Every sufficiently small smooth deformation preserving Bergman logarithmic flatness is induced by a holomorphic automorphism and a constant rescaling. This establishes a Bergman analogue of the local rigidity results for Szeg\H{o} logarithmic flatness obtained by Lu--Tian (Duke Math. J., 2004) and, more recently, Loi--Palmieri--Zuddas (2026).
item.dc:creator: Zhiqin Lu, Yuang Shi

item.title: Contravariant Koszul duality between non-positive and positive dg algebras
item.description: arXiv:2409.08842v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study contravariant Koszul duality between locally finite non-positive and positive dg algebras. We characterize a finiteness condition on the positive side, called pvd-finiteness, in terms of Hom-finiteness of the perfectly valued derived category, local finiteness of the Koszul dual, and the existence of an injective cogenerator in the canonical heart. Under this condition, Koszul duality exchanges perfect and perfectly valued derived categories, and it gives a bijection between quasi-isomorphism classes of locally finite non-positive and pvd-finite positive dg algebras. We also show that the derived category of a pvd-finite positive dg algebra is co-approximable in the sense of Rahul, and that the perfect and perfectly valued derived categories of such an algebra determine each other through finite cohomological functors. As applications, we give a Morita-type characterization of these triangulated categories and show that a bounded heart of such a category is a length category if and only if it is functorially finite.
item.dc:creator: Riku Fushimi

item.title: A torsion theoretic interpretation for sheaves of modules and Grothendieck topologies on directed categories
item.description: arXiv:2506.08685v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every Grothendieck topology induces a hereditary torsion pair in the category of presheaves of modules on a ringed site, and obtain a homological characterization of sheaves of modules: a presheaf of modules is a sheaf of modules if and only if it is saturated with respect to torsion presheaves, or equivalently, it is right perpendicular to torsion presheaves in the sense of Geigle and Lenzing. We also study Grothendieck topologies on directed categories $\mathscr{C}$ satisfying certain finiteness condition, and show that every Grothendieck topology on $\mathscr{C}$ is a subcategory topology if and only if $\mathscr{C}$ is an artinian EI category. Consequently, in this case every sheaf category is equivalent to the presheaf category over a full subcategory of $\mathscr{C}$. Finally, we classify all Grothendieck topologies on a special type of noetherian EI categories, and extend the locally self-injective property of representations of $\mathrm{F}$ and $\mathrm{VI}$ to representations of their infinite full subcategories. Some potential applications in group representation theory are given at the end of this paper.
item.dc:creator: Zhenxing Di, Liping Li, Li Liang

item.title: Standard modules and Dold--Kan correspondences for generalized Reedy categories
item.description: arXiv:2607.12499v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a representation-theoretic approach to generalized Reedy categories through a systematic study of standard modules. For a broad class of these categories, we provide a uniform, computable framework that reduces abstract Hom-spaces between standard modules to elementary linear algebra and graph theory via incidence matrices and morphism fibers. As a primary application, we establish a uniform extension of the Dold--Kan correspondence for certain categories arising from rooted trees, and obtain an orthogonal decomposition for finite spiders, including the category of finite sets and partial injections. Crucially, this machinery unifies and provides a single conceptual framework for several classical, seemingly disparate results across algebraic topology and representation theory, including Kuhn's decomposition theorem for vector spaces and the Th\'evenaz--Webb semisimplicity theorem for Mackey functors.
item.dc:creator: Liping Li

item.title: Square root crystals and the square root of $B(\infty)$
item.description: arXiv:2608.11009v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a general monoidal category of $\mathbf{N}$-root crystals and then study the special case of square root $\mathfrak{gl}_n$-crystals. The latter objects include Yu's crystals on semistandard set-valued tableaux. Prior work of the first author, Tong, and Yu showed that regular square root $\mathfrak{gl}_n$-crystals can be a useful tool for proving Grothendieck positivity results. The objects studied here go beyond the regular case and allow us to construct a square root analog of the direct limit crystal $B(\infty)$. We give several descriptions of our square root of $B(\infty)$, using marginally large tableaux, the Lusztig or PBW parameterization, and the Nakashima--Zelevinsky polyhedral model. We show that this crystal has a simple character formula, exhibits a nontrivial Demazure filtration, and recovers Yu's semistandard set-valued tableau crystals after taking appropriate tensor products. We also investigate a number of differences between square root crystals and classical crystal constructions.
item.dc:creator: Eric Marberg, Travis Scrimshaw

item.title: A Proof of the Second brick-Brauer-Thrall Conjecture for $E$-infinite algebras
item.description: arXiv:2609.31417v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For any finite-dimensional algebra $A$ over an algebraically closed field, we prove that if $A$ is $E$-infinite, then the Second brick-Brauer-Thrall Conjecture holds for $A$. In fact, we show that if there is a rational ray outside the $\tau$-tilting fan of $A$, then $A$ admits an infinite family of $\theta$-stable bricks of dimension $d$, for some positive integer $d$ and weight $\theta$. To show our main result, from any $\tau$-regular component of $A$ with no dense orbit, we obtain a brick component that also has no dense orbit and whose points in general position are $\theta$-stable modules for a given weight $\theta$. As an important consequence, we conclude that $A$ is stably-discrete (also called multiplicity-free) if and only if $A$ is $E$-finite. Moreover, we prove that Demonet's (lattice point) Conjecture implies the stable Second brick-Brauer-Thrall Conjecture. For $E$-infinite algebras, our results settle several open conjectures. Together with our earlier work and recent developments, this leads to important reductions in the study of some challenging open problems.
item.dc:creator: Kaveh Mousavand, Charles Paquette

item.title: The Benson--Etingof--Ostrik conjecture for finite tensor categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.04096v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every finite symmetric tensor category over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic admits a symmetric tensor functor to a higher Verlinde category. This was conjectured for arbitrary symmetric tensor categories of moderate growth by Benson, Etingof and Ostrik. The proof uses higher Frobenius functors, introduced by the authors in [CF1]. The main effort is directed towards a proof of a conjecture from [CF1] about thick tensor ideals in the representation category of elementary abelian $p$-groups, which implies that the higher Frobenius functors are symmetric monoidal. In fact, we prove a refinement of the latter conjecture that relates tensoring with restricted Steinberg modules to an iterated generalised cohomology of modules of elementary abelian $p$-groups.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Coulembier, Johannes Flake

item.title: Young's lattice, invariant ideals, and weak identities
item.description: arXiv:2610.36638v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a $d$-dimensional vector space $V$ over a field of characteristic zero, we show that $GL(V)$-stable ideals of the universal enveloping algebra of the free two-step nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak n_2(V)$ are in natural correspondence with filters in Young's lattice of integer partitions with at most $d$ rows. The same classification holds for $GL(V)$-stable Poisson ideals of $S(V\oplus\Lambda^2(V))$ with its natural Poisson bracket. As applications, we determine all weak polynomial identities of the $n$-th Weyl algebra relative to its standard generating subspace and of the universal enveloping algebra of the $(2n+1)$-dimensional Heisenberg Lie algebra relative to the Lie algebra itself.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Dotsenko, Artem Lopatin

item.title: The quantum double of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$
item.description: arXiv:2607.10602v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we construct the quantum double $D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ of the restricted quantum group $\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2})$. We describe the algebraic structure of $D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ by generators and relations. Moreover, we give the comultiplication $\Delta$, the counit $\varepsilon$ and the antipode $S$, respectively. Finally, we classify all irreducible representations of $D(\mathbf{\overline{u}}_q(\mathfrak{sl_2}))$ when $p=2$.
item.dc:creator: Hua Sun, Yijie Shen, Xiaoming Li, Huixiang Chen

item.title: Cutoff for q-deformed classical card shuffles in the type A Iwahori--Hecke algebra
item.description: arXiv:2609.13570v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the mixing behavior of three q-deformed card shuffles on $\mathcal{H}_q(S_n)$: the short systematic scan introduced in \cite{DiaconisRam2000}, the $q$--deformed random--to--random shuffle introduced in \cite{AxelrodFreedBraunerChiangComminsLang2024}, and the $q$--deformed $k$--star transposition shuffle, whose $q=1$ counterpart was studied in \cite{ArfaeeNestoridi}. The first two chains were diagonalized in \cite{DiaconisRam2000} and \cite{AxelrodFreedBraunerChiangComminsLang2024}, respectively. Here, we diagonalize the $q$--deformed $k$--star transposition shuffle and use the spectra of the three chains to study their mixing behavior. For fixed $q>1$, we prove that all three exhibit total variation and $\ell^2$ cutoff. For the short systematic scan, these improve both the upper and lower bounds of Diaconis and Ram \cite{DiaconisRam2000}.
item.dc:creator: Samira Arfaee, Bryan Wong

item.title: The commuting scheme of $\mathfrak{g}_2$ and a degree formula for commuting schemes
item.description: arXiv:2610.05018v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Over a field of characteristic zero, we show that the commuting scheme of the exceptional Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}_2$ is Cohen-Macaulay and normal (in particular, reduced). We determine its Hilbert series, show that it has degree $1825$ and is not Gorenstein, and determine an explicit linear system of parameters. A crucial ingredient of (one of) our proofs is a root theoretic formula for the degree of the commuting scheme of any reductive Lie algebra whose Borel subalgebra has a complete-intersection commuting scheme, which includes all classical Lie algebras of small rank as well as $E_6$ and $G_2$. Finally, we give a criterion that implies Cohen-Macaulayness and reducedness of the commuting scheme in any given positive characteristic and use it to show that the commuting scheme is Cohen-Macaulay and reduced for every prime $5\leq p\leq1000$. We also resolve the `bad' characteristic cases and show that the commuting scheme is reduced and Cohen-Macaulay over fields of characteristic $3$, and reduced but not Cohen-Macaulay over fields of characteristic $2$ where it has degree $438$.
item.dc:creator: Pallav Goyal
